Asymmetric Aza-Claisen Rearrangement between Enantioenriched
α‑Chiral Allylamines and Allenones
Rui-Han Dai, Qi Wang, Zhi-Xiong Chen, and Shi-Kai Tian *
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2021, 86, 3065 −3073 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: An unprecedented asymmetric aza-Claisen rearrangement between
enantioenriched α-chiral allylamines and allenones was found to proceed in the
absence of catalysts and additives at room temperature. The rearrangement,
followed by hydrolysis, provides convenient access to structurally diverse δ-chiral
β-diketones in good to excellent yields with excellent retention of enantiopurity.
This protocol proved powerful for the construction of an all-carbon quaternary
stereocenter with high enantiopurity.
T
he aza-Claisen rearrangement of allylamines is a versatile
C−N bond cleavage reaction that serves as a key step in
the construction of complex nitrogen-containing molecules. 1
Charge acceleration has been frequently employed as a
powerful strategy to decrease the reaction temperature via
converting allylamines into the corresponding ammonium salts
through protonation, Lewis acid coordination, or quaterniza-
tion prior to the aza-Claisen rearrangement. Particularly,
zwitterionic aza-Claisen rearrangements can proceed under
relatively mild conditions after nucleophilic addition of tertiary
allylamines to π-electrophiles such as 2-alkynoates,
2 acetylenic
sulfones,3 allenoates,4 ketenes,5,6 ketenimines,7 carbodiimides,
isocyanates, and isothiocyanates. 8 While stereochemical
advantages can be expected from the aza-Claisen rearrange-
ments because of their chair-like six-membered transition
states with minimized repulsive interactions, only
L-(−)-pro-
line-derived α-chiral allylamines have been reported previously
to exhibit e ﬀective 1,3-chirality transfer in the ketene-mediated
rearrangement/ring-expansion reaction ( Scheme 1 a).5d,e,g To
our knowledge, 1,3-chirality transfer has not yet been disclosed
for the aza-Claisen rearrangement of other types of
enantioenriched α-chiral allylamines, which, though, can be
readily accessible by resolution of the racemic ones with
inexpensive chiral acids.
9 In connection with our exploration of
new reactions of electrophile-activated tertiary amines, 10 we
have developed an unprecedented asymmetric zwitterionic aza-
Claisen rearrangement be tween enantioenriched α-chiral
allylamines and allenones in the absence of catalysts and
additives at room temperature ( Scheme 1 b). Importantly, the
rearrangement, followed by hydrolysis, provides convenient
access to structurally diverse δ-chiral β-diketones with excellent
retention of enantiopurity.
Inspired by previous reports on the zwitterionic aza-Claisen
rearrangements of π-electrophile-activated tertiary allyl-
amines,
2−8 we initiated our investigation on a possible
asymmetric aza-Claisen rearrangement between enantioen-
riched α-chiral allylamines and allenones, 11 wherein retention
of enantiopurity was expected via a chair-like six-membered
transition state with minimized repulsive interactions ( Scheme
1b). To our delight, simply treating allylamine rac-1a with
allenone 2a in dichloromethane at room temperature a ﬀorded
β-amino enone rac-3a in 85% NMR yield ( Table 1, entry 1). It
is noteworthy that the disubstituted alkene moiety was formed
with exclusive E selectivity, which is in line with the
mechanism involving a privileged chair-like six-membered
transition state as shown in Scheme 1 b. We next screened a

Since β-amino enone rac-3a was hydrolyzed partially when
being puri ﬁed by silica gel chromatography, we removed
methanol from the reaction mixture of allylamine rac-1a and
allenone 2a under reduced pressure at room temperature and
then treated the residue with silica gel in dichloromethane,
which contained 1.0% (v/v) water. This protocol a ﬀorded δ-
branched β-diketone rac-4a in 95% yield ( Table 2 , entry 1).
Next, we surveyed the e ﬀects of the N-substituent in the
allylamine on the aza-Claisen rearrangement. In general, the
reaction with an N,N-dialkyl allylamine gave a much better
yield than that with a less nucleophilic allylamine bearing an N-
aryl group ( Table 2 , entries 1 −6). Not surprisingly, the aza-
Claisen rearrangement was not observed in the corresponding
reaction of either secondary allylamine rac-1ag or primary
allylamine rac-1ah under the standard conditions ( Table 2 ,
entries 7 and 8).
Encouraged by the above results, we examined an
asymmetric version of the aza-Claisen rearrangement. Treat-
ment of enantioenriched α-chiral allylamine 1a (97% ee) with
allenone 2a, followed by hydrolysis at room temperature,
aﬀorded δ-chiral β-diketone 4a with complete retention of
enantiopurity ( Table 3 , entry 1). The protocol for sequential
aza-Claisen rearrangement and hydrolysis was successfully
extended to a variety of enantioenriched polysubstituted α-
chiral allylamines, and structurally diverse δ-chiral β-diketones
were obtained in good to excellent yields with excellent
retention of enantiopurity ( Table 3, entries 2
−11). Notably, in
these cases, the di- and trisubstituted alkene moieties were

proved powerful for the construction of an all-carbon
quaternary stereocenter with high enantiopurity ( Table 3 ,
entry 10). We also examined ( S)-(+)-carvone-derived α-chiral
allylamine 1l and obtained δ-chiral β-diketone 4l with excellent
diastereoselectivity ( Table 3 , entry 12).
On the other hand, the aza-Claisen rearrangement worked
well with a range of allenones bearing a monosubstituted
allenyl group, including 1-aryl-, 1-heteroaryl-, 1-alkenyl-, and 1-
alkylbuta-2,3-dien-1-ones ( Table 4 ). In these cases, the
reaction exhibited complete retention of enantiopurity and
the alkene moieties were formed with exclusive E selectivity.
Nevertheless, the reaction did not occur with bulkier allenones
such as 2-methyl-1-phenylbuta-2,3-dien-1-one ( 2k) and 4-
methyl-1-phenylpen ta-2,3-dien-1-one ( 2l). Moreover, the
absolute con ﬁguration of δ-chiral β-diketone 4o was assigned
to be S by X-ray crystallography and the stereochemistry for its
formation is in line with the mechanism of 1,3-chirality transfer
involving a chair-like six-membered transition state as depicted
in Scheme 1 b.
In summary, we have developed an e ﬃcient asymmetric aza-
Claisen rearrangement be tween enantioenriched α-chiral
allylamines and allenones in the absence of catalysts and
additives at room temperature. The rearrangement, followed
by hydrolysis, provides convenient access to structurally
diverse δ-chiral β-diketones in good to excellent yields with
excellent retention of enantiopurity. In these cases, the di- and
trisubstituted alkene moieties were formed with exclusive E
selectivity. Moreover, this protocol proved powerful for the
construction of an all-carbon quaternary stereocenter with high
enantiopurity.
